summary: Lens-diverse task review of one diff, each finding adversarially verified by a skeptic panel

prior_findings.note: Stack.kafka_lag (e2e.py:621-625) now calls _consumer_lag(stdout, stderr, group) (469-474). That function looks for 'does not exist' on either stream and parses the table from stdout only. parse_consumer_groups_describe (423-466) skips any row whose PARTITION is not numeric, whose offsets are not digits or '-', or whose GROUP is a different group. I probed CLI-shaped output with real CONSUMER-ID/HOST/CLIENT-ID columns and a '-' committed offset. Results: stable gives {topic: 9}; Empty with the stderr notice gives 9; rebalancing with the stderr notice gives 9; 'Error: Consumer group ... does not exist.' on stdout gives a ValueError saying the group does not exist. The new tests drive Stack.kafka_lag through a stub compose with the table on stdout and the notice on stderr. One case raises 'no GROUP table': an Empty group with no committed offsets, where the CLI prints only the stderr notice. That raise is conservative and consistent with the docstring, which says lag 0 is never claimed, so it is not a regression.

gen_e2e_env.py:91-92 FILE_MODES sets every *.crt to 0644 and both *.key files to 0600, and _write_certs applies it per file (308-309). Readers checked: docker image inspect shows Config.User empty for mailpit (entrypoint /mailpit) and for postgres:16-alpine, so both key readers run as root. No compose file sets cap_drop, cap_add, user or security_opt, so root keeps DAC override. pg_tls_entrypoint.sh copies the key as root, chowns it to postgres and sets 0600 before docker-entrypoint steps down. The CAs (e2e-ca.crt on the nine app services, postgres-ca.crt on the app services and migrate) are 0644, so the uid 1000 appuser can read them under a runner uid of 1001. A recorded-chmod test covers this, plus a POSIX-only real-mode test (skipped on Windows).

tests/e2e/conftest.py:84 adds pytest.mark.timeout(900, func_only=True). In the installed pytest-timeout, _parse_marker reads the func_only kwarg, and runtest_protocol arms the timer only when func_only is False. No test under tests/e2e sets its own timeout marker, and pytest.ini has no timeout options. I confirmed this empirically with a scratch session fixture that sleeps 4 s under a 2 s marker. func_only=True gave '2 passed'; without func_only the run reported 'Timeout' and exit 1.
Same fix and evidence as WS054-HAR-2: the default marker bounds only the test function, so the setup phase that builds the stack is no longer covered.

_strict_operator_values now runs at gen_e2e_env.py:349-352, before the foreign-dir check, mkdir, _restrict_dir, the marker write and _write_certs. It is passed {**values, **dict.fromkeys(sources, '')}. That is equivalent to the old post-generation call, because no non-secret registry row uses REDIS_URL, E2E_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD or an UNSET secret as its source. A strict generation against the real registry exits 0 in a probe. The new test asserts exit 2 and that no run dir exists.

(a) The fresh-interpreter test also asserts that COMPOSE_FILES[-1] is the overlay. A new test feeds _image_refs the real overlay text with a distinct digest and expects that digest back, so the fallback can no longer mask the result. (b) A new assertion checks that the '$$'-unescaped value of every e2e.env entry is absent from stdout+stderr. All of these pass in the scoped run (67 passed, 1 skipped).

parse_provision_output (e2e.py:488-493) treats a line without '=' as None. It shows a key only when it fullmatches [a-z_]{1,40}, and every other line as '<unexpected line>'. A JSON log line, a ':' separator line and a token before '=' (the key would contain ':', '/' or uppercase) therefore never reach the error. The JSON-line and colon cases were added to the parametrized test.

_expect (867-869) now reports only _response_summary. For a JSON detail list that is type and loc, filtered to safe character classes (input and msg are dropped); otherwise it is the content type and byte count. Grep finds no remaining response.text or body echo in e2e.py. Tests check the HopFailure text for a FastAPI 422 with the token and password in input, a 200 carrying tokens, and a plain 500 body.

_remove_run_dir (161-170) deletes only a directory that holds a regular-file RUN_MARKER or is empty, and both _start and _teardown (including the CLI 'down') use it. The generator writes the marker only into a new, empty or already-marked DIR (358-370). I probed this on Windows. A junction run dir resolves to its foreign target and is refused. Calling it directly on the unresolved junction is refused with a RuntimeError. A junction to a marked dir is refused by rmtree ('Cannot call rmtree on a symbolic link'). A marked dir holding an inner junction is removed while the foreign target stays intact. A marker that is a directory is refused. _check_run_dir refuses the repo (including case, trailing-dot, trailing-space and \\.\ spellings), '.', '..', 'tests', drive-relative 'C:' and 'D:', drive and UNC share roots, home and '~'. The \\?\ and \\localhost\D$ spellings of the repo or home get past the path check. The marker check still refuses those directories (non-empty, no marker), and anything the generator would write inside the repo is gitignored (*.env, secrets/), so deletion stays confined to generator-made runs.

test_mvp_039_compose_errors_are_scrubbed_of_every_generated_secret runs _compose and compose_config against a stub argv that leaks known values on stderr and on stdout. It expects exactly 4 '***', no full or partial value, and the public value kept. test_mvp_039_no_registry_secret_is_treated_as_public compares the registry's secret sources with _PUBLIC_ENV_KEYS. I recomputed this: 19 secret sources, no overlap (ENCRYPTION_RETIRED_KEYS_JSON was removed from the public set). In generated dev and strict e2e.env files, every secret key present is in _hidden_values except ENCRYPTION_RETIRED_KEYS_JSON, whose value is the literal '{}' (length 2). The two absent sources are the documented unset ones, AUTH_PRIVATE_KEY_PEM and LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The call() and sql() error paths still have no test of their own, but they call _scrub(_hidden_values(...)) directly.
Same fix and evidence as WS054-SEC-3: StackConfig resolves and checks run_dir, and every harness deletion goes through the marker-or-empty guard in _remove_run_dir.
